correctness.rationale: For \(d\ge2\) and positive edge lengths, width and hyperplane brightness along the same spherical normal are weighted sums of absolute coordinates. The Dirichlet beta integrals give one- and two-coordinate moments and exactly \(\operatorname{Cov}(W,B)=V(1-2/\pi-\beta_d Q)\); negative coordinate covariance gives \(\beta_d>0\). The scale-free \(Q\) statistic is a strictly convex sum of exponentials in the free logarithmic edge coordinates at fixed aspect ratio. Reflection and Jensen identify the sharp geometric-mean minimum; maximum at a binary vertex with balanced groups gives the sharp two-level maximum. Continuity, strict monotonicity and gamma asymptotics give the complete two-threshold sign regimes including \(d=2\). Each implication is proved in RESULT.md. value.rationale: The theorem resolves a natural coupled geometric statistic: directional thickness and orthogonal shadow hyperarea of the same randomly oriented box can be positively or negatively correlated. For every dimension it completely classifies the sign at fixed anisotropy, with sharp thresholds, all equality configurations and a genuine coexistence interval, and identifies distinct \(O(1)\) versus \(O(d^2)\) aspect-ratio scales. This is more than a cheap sign example or a known-table recomputation. The finite checker contributes reproducibility, not intrinsic value.
